name: chat-gpt
title: ChatGPT
description: Animated ChatGPT composer that types a prompt and morphs the voice button into a send button
useFor: Announcing a ChatGPT integration or GPT-powered feature where the OpenAI brand must be recognizable.
avoidFor: The product being demoed is Claude — use `claude-chat` instead to match Anthropic's UI and warm color palette.

name: claude-chat
title: Claude Chat
description: Animated Claude chat input that types a prompt and morphs the waveform button into a send button
useFor: Announcing a Claude integration or Anthropic-powered feature where the Claude brand must be visible.
avoidFor: The product is Claude Code CLI — use `claude-code` instead, which shows the terminal welcome screen with `cwd` and agent context.

name: claude-code
title: Claude Code
description: Animated Claude Code CLI welcome screen that types a command into the terminal prompt
useFor: Depicting a Claude Code / agentic-CLI workflow as a recognizable branded surface in a dev-tool demo.
avoidFor: You need a generic, unbranded terminal — use `terminal-simulator`.

name: opencode
title: OpenCode
description: Animated OpenCode TUI welcome screen that types a query into the input
useFor: Depicting the OpenCode TUI as a recognizable branded surface in a dev-tool demo.
avoidFor: You're depicting a different product — use the matching card (`claude-code`, `v0`, `chat-gpt`, `claude-chat`).

name: v0
title: v0
description: Animated Vercel v0 composer that types a prompt and morphs the mic button into a send button
useFor: Depicting the Vercel v0 composer as a recognizable branded surface in a generative-UI demo.
avoidFor: You're depicting a different product — use the matching card (`chat-gpt`, `claude-chat`, `claude-code`, `opencode`).

name: ecosystem-constellation
title: Ecosystem Constellation
description: A central product logo orbited by integration satellites with pulsing data lines
useFor: The story is "we plug into everything" — one hub product ringed by the tools it connects to.
avoidFor: You need your own integration logos; the eight marks are hardcoded in the file, so swapping them means editing the copied component.

name: infinite-bento-pan
title: Infinite Bento Pan
description: A hypnotic diagonal camera glide over an oversized grid of bento cards
useFor: You need an ambient establishing shot that says "a lot is happening here" without asking anyone to read a single number.
avoidFor: The figures on screen have to mean something — every counter, stat and chart here is sine-driven filler, so use `animated-line-chart` or `animated-bar-chart` for a number the viewer should actually read.

name: live-code-compilation
title: Live Code Compilation
description: A split-screen where code is typed on the left and the right-side UI snaps to match in a single frame
useFor: You want to show cause and effect for a developer audience: a style prop finishes typing on the left and the button on the right changes on that exact frame.
avoidFor: The code on screen has to be yours — the eight typed fragments and the resulting button are hardcoded, while `glass-code-block` and `glass-code-walk` take arbitrary code as a `code` prop.

name: confetti
title: Confetti
description: Deterministic confetti burst for Remotion — seeded particles with gravity, spin, and flutter
useFor: A milestone moment needs a celebratory payoff — product launch, plan completion, success screen.
avoidFor: The video has a clean, minimal, or corporate tone — confetti reads as celebration-specific and breaks professional pacing; use a subtle shader backdrop like `shader-grain-gradient` instead.

name: crumple-toss
title: Crumple Toss
description: Crushes an element into a ball of paper and throws it out of frame
useFor: Discarding something on screen — the old plan, the wrong answer, the previous version.
avoidFor: You want a general element exit in a clean UI scene — this one is loud and physical; use a fade instead.

name: cursor-gravity
title: Cursor Gravity
description: A rounded triangular cursor tugs a button out of the screen edge with pulsed elastic resistance
useFor: An empty scene should reveal a call to action through a physical pulling gesture.
avoidFor: A cursor must accurately demonstrate an existing interface — use simulated-cursor.

name: ink-arrow
title: Ink Arrow
description: A hand-drawn arrow that draws itself from one point to another in stop-motion poses
useFor: A hand-drawn annotation should point from one thing to another — callouts over paper or scrapbook scenes.
avoidFor: You need a straight technical connector or a diagram edge — this is a wobbly pen line with a personality, not a flowchart arrow.

name: paper-wobble
title: Paper Wobble
description: Per-pose reshoot jitter that makes any content feel hand-placed on a desk
useFor: Any block should carry the stop-motion reshoot wobble — headlines, cards, or content that must feel hand-placed rather than laid out.
avoidFor: The content should sit rock-still — UI simulations, code blocks being read.

name: radial-burst
title: Radial Burst
description: Sculptural ribbons twist into a tilted ring and sweep outward through layered contour echoes
useFor: A product introduction needs a short abstract geometric opening before its title.
avoidFor: The effect should celebrate an action with scattered particles — use `confetti`.

name: scribble-circle
title: Scribble Circle
description: A brush circle that sweeps itself around a region of the frame, opening thin and closing thick
useFor: Circling the one element that matters — a button, a number, a row in a screenshot.
avoidFor: You need a permanent border or a focus ring. This is a gesture that happens once, not a state.

name: simulated-cursor
title: Simulated Cursor
description: A synthetic mouse cursor that travels between waypoints and fires a click ripple, for narrating a UI on screen
useFor: You are narrating a screen demo and need a synthetic cursor that moves predictably over a UI screenshot or recording
avoidFor: You need a real screen recording — this draws a synthetic overlay, not a capture of actual mouse movement

name: tv-power-off
title: TV Power Off
description: End a scene the way a tube does — the picture collapses into a glowing line, pinches to a phosphor dot, and the frame is left dead black
useFor: A scene should end like a device being switched off rather than fading out — the picture collapses, a dot lingers, and the frame is dead.
avoidFor: The tube look should hold for the whole scene instead of ending it — use `crt-screen`, which is a sustained filter with no duration of its own.

name: backdrop
title: Backdrop
description: Full-frame fill with an optional rounded, shadowed content frame — accepts a color, gradient, image, or any React element as a live animated background
useFor: You need a scene background — wrap every composition in `Backdrop` rather than hardcoding background colors on individual components.
avoidFor: You need an infinitely looping ambient background as a standalone track — use a shader backdrop directly and let the composition handle framing.

name: chat-to-preview-layout
title: Chat to Preview Layout
description: A two-column split where the chat column shrinks and the preview column expands, for showing an agent building something
useFor: Showing an AI agent at work — the conversation starts as the subject, then yields the frame to what it produced
avoidFor: Both columns should stay the same size — this component exists for the ratio change; use a plain flex row

name: drift
title: Drift
description: Wrap any scene in a slow camera push-in so no frame is ever static
useFor: Any static scene should feel alive — hero cards, feature panels, dashboards sitting between transitions.
avoidFor: The content is already animated with strong motion — layering drift on top of it doubles the movement and muddies the read.

name: stage
title: Stage
description: Put a screenshot, recording, or long page on a perspective studio plane and direct the camera across it with timeline keyframes
useFor: A product screen, website, image, or live React scene should read as a photographed object rather than a flat full-frame capture.
avoidFor: You only need a full-frame fill or rounded inset with no 3D presentation — use `backdrop`.

name: shader-caustics
title: Caustics
description: A field of refracted light — the bright filaments light makes through a rippling surface
useFor: Water, light, or premium ambient backdrops where refracted-light filaments fit the mood.
avoidFor: You want structured cellular noise — use `shader-voronoi`.

name: shader-color-panels
title: Color Panels
description: Overlapping translucent color panels sliding past each other
useFor: You want an architectural, glassy backdrop of translucent panes sliding past each other.
avoidFor: You want organic, flowing motion — use `shader-warp` or `shader-metaballs`.

name: shader-dithering
title: Dithering
description: Ordered-dither shading over an animated gradient field
useFor: You want a retro/print, 1-bit ordered-dither texture over a moving gradient.
avoidFor: You want a centered dithered sphere — override `shape` (this wrapper defaults to full-bleed `"wave"`).

name: shader-dot-orbit
title: Dot Orbit
description: Dots orbiting on concentric paths across the frame
useFor: You want a structured dot-grid backdrop with gentle orbital motion.
avoidFor: You want a static dot grid — the static `dot-grid` shader is intentionally not shipped; use a CSS grid.

name: shader-gem-smoke
title: Gem Smoke
description: Animated color fields flowing behind and inside a glassy logo silhouette
useFor: Brand or logo reveals that want smoke living inside and around a mark.
avoidFor: You have no logo or mark to feed as `image` — use `shader-smoke-ring` or `shader-neuro-noise` for a shapeless field instead.

name: shader-god-rays
title: God Rays
description: Volumetric light rays radiating from an off-screen source
useFor: A hero or reveal scene wants cinematic volumetric light rays from a corner source.
avoidFor: The brief bans decorative glow — this is a genuine volumetric shader, but keep `bloom`/`intensity` restrained so it does not read as an AI-slop glow.

name: shader-grain-gradient
title: Grain Gradient
description: Grainy multi-stop gradient that drifts slowly with film-grain texture over the blend
useFor: A gradient backdrop needs analog texture — the grain reads as film/print rather than flat digital.
avoidFor: You need crisp, clean color with no texture — use `shader-mesh-gradient`.

name: shader-light-tunnel
title: Light Tunnel
description: Fly straight through the original OpenShaders hero field mapped into a light tunnel
useFor: A title reveal or product intro needs a luminous forward flight through a tunnel.
avoidFor: A quiet background should leave attention on dense UI — use `shader-mesh-gradient`.

name: shader-liquid-metal
title: Liquid Metal
description: Molten metallic surface with flowing specular highlights
useFor: A premium, industrial, or luxury scene wants a brushed/molten metal surface.
avoidFor: You want a centered metallic emblem — override `shape` back to a paper shape (this wrapper defaults to full-bleed `"none"`).

name: shader-mesh-gradient
title: Mesh Gradient
description: WebGL mesh gradient backdrop driven per-frame for deterministic Remotion renders
useFor: You need a quality, production-grade gradient backdrop.
avoidFor: You want a structured, geometric background — use `shader-dot-orbit` or `shader-voronoi`.

name: shader-metaballs
title: Metaballs
description: Organic blobs merging and splitting like lava
useFor: A playful or organic scene wants lava-lamp blobs merging and splitting.
avoidFor: The brand is strictly serious/corporate — metaballs read playful.

name: shader-neuro-noise
title: Neuro Noise
description: Organic neural-web noise field that slowly morphs
useFor: An AI / ML / tech scene wants an organic neural-web texture that reads as "intelligence".
avoidFor: You want smooth cloud noise instead of web filaments — use `shader-perlin-noise` or `shader-simplex-noise`.

name: shader-perlin-noise
title: Perlin Noise
description: Classic Perlin noise clouds drifting across the frame
useFor: You want a soft, cloudy, organic backdrop that drifts slowly and stays calm.
avoidFor: You want a smoother, more flowing field — use `shader-simplex-noise`.

name: shader-pulsing-border
title: Pulsing Border
description: Glowing border frame that pulses around the edges
useFor: You want a pulsing lit frame around the scene edges to contain foreground content.
avoidFor: The brief bans decorative glow — keep `bloom`/`intensity` restrained so the border does not read as AI-slop neon.

name: shader-simplex-noise
title: Simplex Noise
description: Simplex noise flow field, smoother than Perlin
useFor: You want the smoothest of the noise backdrops — fewer directional artifacts than Perlin.
avoidFor: You want cloudier, softer fog — use `shader-perlin-noise`.

name: shader-smoke-ring
title: Smoke Ring
description: Soft smoke ring curling and dissipating in place
useFor: You want a single soft, centered smoke ring as a focal atmospheric element.
avoidFor: You need a full-bleed edge-to-edge texture — this is a centered object; use a noise or gradient shader.

name: shader-spiral
title: Spiral
description: Rotating spiral arms radiating from the center
useFor: You want a hypnotic, rotating radial background with visible arm structure.
avoidFor: You want closed concentric rings rather than open arms — use `shader-swirl`.

name: shader-strata
title: Strata
description: Fine horizontal sediment layers displaced by fbm noise, each drifting at its own depth
useFor: Calm, grounded, geological ambient backdrops — foundations, stability, "built on" narratives.
avoidFor: You want motion with a clear direction or flow — use `shader-warp`.

name: shader-swirl
title: Swirl
description: Concentric bands swirling around a center point
useFor: You want a hypnotic, radial background with clear banded structure around a center.
avoidFor: You want free-flowing liquid folds rather than concentric bands — use `shader-warp`.

name: shader-voronoi
title: Voronoi
description: Animated Voronoi cells shifting and re-tessellating
useFor: You want a cellular, crystalline backdrop that shifts and re-tessellates.
avoidFor: You want soft, structureless fog — use `shader-perlin-noise` or `shader-simplex-noise`.

name: shader-warp
title: Warp
description: Domain-warped color field that folds and stretches like liquid
useFor: A hero scene wants organic, liquid motion that feels alive but stays out of the way.
avoidFor: Text legibility over the whole frame is critical — raise `softness` and keep `distortion` low, or use a solid `backdrop`.

name: shader-water
title: Water
description: Caustic water-surface ripples with subtle refraction
useFor: A scene wants a calm, aquatic atmosphere with gentle refracted highlights.
avoidFor: The palette must be warm or vibrant — water reads cool by design; recolor via `colorHighlight`/`colorBack` or choose another shader.

name: shader-weave
title: Weave
description: A woven substrate of warp and weft threads crossing on a domain-warped grid
useFor: Tactile, crafted, "made-of" textures — fabric, mesh, or substrate metaphors.
avoidFor: You want a smooth gradient field — use `shader-mesh-gradient`.

name: github-sponsors
title: GitHub Sponsors
description: Animated GitHub Sponsors lockup — a self-drawing heart that docks to a header, every sponsor avatar blur-staggering into a grid, then a thank-you headline and a CTA
useFor: A thank-you beat for funders — the heart draws itself, docks upward, and every sponsor avatar blur-staggers into a grid beneath it.
avoidFor: The milestone is a star count rather than funding — use `github-stars`, whose odometer counts up to a total.

name: github-stars
title: GitHub Stars
description: Stargazer list fly-through with a synced odometer counter — renders standalone from sample data or accepts live stargazer props
useFor: Celebrating an OSS milestone — the count-up odometer landing on a star total is the payoff beat.
avoidFor: You only need the number to roll up without the stargazer fly-through — use `number-wheel` or `rolling-number`.

name: logo-enter
title: Logo Enter
description: A stacked group of round brand chips that spring in one-by-one, then hold
useFor: Showing a cluster of brand/partner/integration logos arriving together ("works with…", an AI-tool lineup, an icon cloud).
avoidFor: You need a single product wordmark lockup — this is a multi-chip cluster, not one mark; build a lightweight lockup or resolve kinetic text (`kinetic-center-build`, `per-character-rise`) into the name.

name: x-follow-card
title: X Follow Card
description: Animated X profile follow card with spring bounce-in, staggered blur-in, and cursor-driven Follow transition
useFor: Showcasing a single X profile with the recognizable click-to-Follow payoff as the action beat.
avoidFor: You're aggregating follower growth or notifications rather than one profile — use `x-followers-overview`.

name: x-followers-overview
title: X Followers Overview
description: X follow notifications flip through in 3D, then the total follower count blurs in
useFor: A milestone or social-proof scene needs cycling follow notifications building to a total reveal.
avoidFor: You're highlighting one profile and a Follow click — use `x-follow-card`.

name: brand-guidelines
title: Brand Guidelines
description: A complete editorial identity film with a color palette, kinetic typography, original object photography, and a geometric brand mark
useFor: You want to introduce a brand system through its mark, colors, typography, and photography.
avoidFor: You need a multi-feature software demo rather than an identity film; use `launch-anything`.

name: fomo-limit-orders
title: Order Flow
description: An independent trading-interface demo with fictional data, amber controls, and precise camera choreography
useFor: You want a complete trading-interface demo built from editable React and SVG layers.
avoidFor: You need a general product launch story; use `launch-anything`.

name: launch-anything
title: Product Showcase
description: An editorial product film with forest-green accents, original photography, and seven editable demos
useFor: You want a complete 26.7-second product film with editable text and demonstrations.
avoidFor: You want to introduce a complete visual identity; use `brand-guidelines`.

name: release-teaser
title: Release Teaser
description: A cinematic release announcement with quiet kinetic typography, a dimensional open-ring mark, and moving edge light
useFor: You want a sixteen-second release announcement built around anticipation and a final brand reveal.
avoidFor: You need to show actual product interactions and workflows; use `launch-anything`.

name: workflow-console
title: Workflow Console
description: An independent release-automation film with typed commands, environment diagrams, and pipeline metrics
useFor: You want a complete 46.8-second CLI or automation demo with editable commands and results.
avoidFor: You only need one scrolling command; use `terminal-cursor-zoom`.

name: blur-out-up
title: Blur Out Up
description: Words arrive clean and depart upward with increasing blur for airy exits
useFor: A title or tagline needs a graceful upward exit before the next scene cuts in.
avoidFor: You want a blurred entrance that resolves to crisp — that is `focus-blur-resolve`, which opens blurry and sharpens in.

name: bottom-up-letters
title: Bottom-Up Letters
description: Letters rise from below in a pronounced staircase, one symbol at a time
useFor: A short punchy word or acronym should land with clear, visible per-character energy.
avoidFor: The text is a full sentence or phrase — the high stagger makes long strings feel sluggish; use `per-character-rise` (faster, more even) or `mask-reveal-up` (line-level) instead.

name: caret-swap
title: Caret Swap
description: A gradient caret expands into a block that consumes the first text, then types the second
useFor: One phrase should be replaced by another through a caret gesture: the cursor swells into a block that eats the old text, collapses back and types the new one.
avoidFor: You only need one phrase typed from empty — use `typewriter`.

name: centered-word-build
title: Centered Word Build
description: Words appear sharply from below while the centered phrase pushes closer on every beat
useFor: A short statement should assemble one word at a time while every visible prefix stays centered and pushes closer.
avoidFor: Each new word should physically drive the existing line aside — use `word-push`.

name: chromatic-wave
title: Chromatic Wave
description: A soft wave travels down through the type; where it crosses, the letters ripple and split into RGB fringes, then settle back to white
useFor: A held title — an album cover, a poster hold, a loop — needs slow, ambient distortion instead of a one-shot entrance.
avoidFor: You need a quick glitch accent rather than a five-second traveling wave — use `rgb-glitch-text`.

name: extrude-pop
title: Extrude Pop
description: A flat word pops up out of the plane on a solid colored 3D body, no camera involved
useFor: A short punchy word — a score, a verdict, a CTA — should land with physical weight, like a stamp rising off the page.
avoidFor: The text is long or small — the extruded body doubles the ink and turns a sentence into mush; keep it to one short word.

name: fade-through
title: Fade Through
description: Old text fades out as new fades in with a soft delay, Material-style
useFor: One label, stat, or short phrase needs to swap cleanly into another in the same slot.
avoidFor: You want the incoming words to arrive one by one — use `per-word-crossfade` for a sequential word-level fade instead.

name: focus-blur-resolve
title: Focus Blur Resolve
description: A premium focus pull from heavy blur to crisp text, then a soft blur-out exit
useFor: A hero word or short phrase should feel like a camera lens pulling into focus.
avoidFor: You want a clean departure upward after a crisp entrance — that arc belongs to `blur-out-up`, which arrives clean and exits with upward blur.

name: fog-rise
title: Fog Rise
description: Display text resolves out of fog center-out, sharpening from heavy blur with vertical streaks
useFor: A big display word should materialize out of atmosphere — already at its size and position, resolving from heavy blur as if rising along the z-axis.
avoidFor: The whole line should sharpen at once without per-character order — use `focus-blur-resolve`.

name: gooey-morph
title: Gooey Morph
description: Bars fly in Tetris-style, land as a row, and melt into a word through a gooey blur-and-threshold morph
useFor: A title reveal should feel liquid and organic — shapes fuse and hand their mass to the word instead of crossfading.
avoidFor: You need a plain text entrance without the shape build-up — use `soft-blur-in` or `mask-reveal-up`.

name: gradient-scale-cut-text
title: Gradient Scale Cut Text
description: An oversized gradient reveal snaps to a compact blurred line that settles into focus
useFor: A title should begin at an imposing scale and resolve through a deliberately abrupt editorial cut.
avoidFor: The scale change must feel continuous — use `scale-down-fade` or `zoom-words`.

name: hand-count
title: Hand Count
description: A number that counts up in stop-motion poses, rewritten by hand at every pose
useFor: A stat, price, or count belongs in a hand-made scene — the number should arrive by being written, not by rolling.
avoidFor: The scene is a slick product UI or a dashboard metric — use `rolling-number` or `number-wheel`, which glide a mechanical typeface.

name: handwrite
title: Handwrite
description: Handwritten text laid down letter by letter on a quantized stop-motion clock
useFor: Captions, labels, and headlines should read as pen-written on paper — the core text voice of stop-motion scrapbook scenes.
avoidFor: You are simulating a terminal or an input being typed into — use `typewriter`.

name: infinite-marquee
title: Infinite Marquee
description: A continuously scrolling horizontal text strip that loops seamlessly
useFor: A scene needs ambient motion in the background or as a decorative band between sections.
avoidFor: The text should enter, hold, then exit — that is a reveal animation, not a ticker; use `blur-out-up` or `mask-reveal-up` instead.

name: ink-underline
title: Ink Underline
description: A hand-dragged ink stroke that draws itself across in a few stop-motion poses
useFor: A hand-dragged ink underline belongs beneath a written headline, URL, or stat — pairs with `handwrite`, with `delay` set from `handwriteDuration`.
avoidFor: You are painting a highlight behind a word inside a sentence — use `marker-highlight`.

name: inline-highlight
title: Inline Highlight
description: Animate one word inside a sentence from a base color to a brand color
useFor: One keyword inside a sentence needs to draw attention through a color shift without any background decoration.
avoidFor: You want a physical drawn marker or filled background behind the word — use `marker-highlight` for a visible paint-stroke effect instead.

name: inline-pill-takeover
title: Inline Pill Takeover
description: A clipped pill expands inside a sentence, pushes the words apart, and takes over the frame
useFor: A sentence should transform an inline placeholder into a CTA without cutting to a separate title card.
avoidFor: Only one phrase should change color without affecting layout — use `inline-highlight`.

name: inline-word-roll
title: Inline Word Roll
description: Switch words beside a fixed prefix with an accelerating vertical roll
useFor: A headline keeps its opening phrase while cycling through audiences, benefits or outcomes.
avoidFor: Every new word should remain in the sentence — use `word-push`.

name: kinetic-center-build
title: Kinetic Center Build
description: Words enter from the right and push the line until the full phrase locks centered
useFor: A short headline should build word by word with satisfying kinetic momentum, locking centered at the end.
avoidFor: The text is long (7+ words) — the centering re-balance on each word becomes distracting; use `line-by-line-slide` for multi-word or multi-line phrases.

name: kinetic-morph-text
title: Kinetic Morph Text
description: Letters lift, rotate, and reshape into the next phrase with delicate outline trails
useFor: A short sequence of phrases should feel like the same letters physically rearranging.
avoidFor: Words should switch with minimal movement — use `per-word-crossfade`.

name: kinetic-warp
title: Kinetic Warp
description: A coarse mesh warp bends a whole word in staccato beats, one axis moving per keyframe
useFor: A short, heavy display word needs a bold kinetic-typography moment where the whole word bends and snaps instead of individual letters animating.
avoidFor: You need a text entrance — the word is fully visible from frame 0 and only distorts; use `tracking-in` or `soft-blur-in` for reveals.

name: line-by-line-slide
title: Line-by-Line Slide
description: Each line slides in from the left with a staggered flow then exits to the right
useFor: A multi-line headline or short paragraph needs a flowing, line-by-line entrance with a matching exit.
avoidFor: The text is a single short phrase — the stagger has nothing to stage; use `mask-reveal-up` or `per-character-rise` for single-line reveals instead.

name: marker-highlight
title: Marker Highlight
description: A colored marker block draws behind a phrase while the text color shifts
useFor: A key phrase inside a sentence needs a physical, hand-drawn-feeling highlight that visually underscores the word.
avoidFor: You want a subtle color-only emphasis with no visible background — use `inline-highlight` for a clean color-shift with no marker block.

name: mask-reveal-up
title: Mask Reveal Up
description: Lines reveal upward with a soft masked feel and compact stagger
useFor: A multi-line headline or stacked list needs a clean, contained upward reveal that holds on screen.
avoidFor: You need an exit animation too — `mask-reveal-up` holds in place after reveal; use `line-by-line-slide` for a reveal that also exits to the right.

name: matrix-decode
title: Matrix Decode
description: Random scramble resolves left-to-right into target text
useFor: A hacker, terminal, or cyberpunk aesthetic is required and the scramble-to-reveal glyph effect is on-brand.
avoidFor: The content is a human sentence or marketing copy — the glitchy scramble reads as broken text to non-technical audiences; use `typewriter` for a clean character-by-character reveal with a more legible progression.

name: micro-scale-fade
title: Micro Scale Fade
description: A calm, tiny scale pop for subtle premium polish on labels and headings
useFor: A label, subheading, or supporting text needs an entrance that feels polished without drawing attention to itself.
avoidFor: The reveal should be the hero moment with visible kinetic weight — use `kinetic-center-build` or `per-character-rise` for entrances that command attention.

name: number-wheel
title: Number Wheel
description: Odometer that rolls a number from one value to another with direction inferred from the values
useFor: A metric, stat, or count should animate to its value in a satisfying odometer roll.
avoidFor: The value is not an integer — this component is designed for whole numbers; format decimals upstream before passing them in.

name: outline-fill-track-text
title: Outline Fill Track Text
description: A rising lead word gives way to an outlined value that fills as one continuous track moves left
useFor: A statement should hand focus from a lead word to a large numeric value in one continuous move.
avoidFor: The two texts should swap in place — use `value-swap` for a compact replacement.

name: per-character-rise
title: Per Character Rise
description: Letters slide up from below with no blur - crisp and kinetic
useFor: A short word or phrase needs a crisp, sharp character-by-character entrance with even, readable stagger.
avoidFor: You want a dramatic staircase effect where each letter visibly lags the previous — use `bottom-up-letters` for the pronounced, wide-gap stagger instead.

name: per-word-crossfade
title: Per-Word Crossfade
description: One phrase fades out as the next fades in, word by word
useFor: Two short phrases need to swap with a soft, word-by-word transition that reads as calm and composed.
avoidFor: The transition should be a single-block fade with no word-level staging — use `fade-through` for a unified opacity swap instead.

name: perspective-marquee
title: Perspective Marquee
description: A 3D-tilted infinite marquee with depth-of-field blur on items rolling toward the horizon
useFor: A dark, cinematic background treatment is needed with text rolling into a 3D vanishing point.
avoidFor: A flat, 2D looping ticker is sufficient — use `infinite-marquee` for a simpler, lighter strip with no perspective transform.

name: perspective-squeeze
title: Perspective Squeeze
description: Two lines of heavy type endlessly trade height while corner-pinned perspective bends the flat stack into receding planes
useFor: A looping hold — an outro, a background title, a stream screen — needs constant, hypnotic typographic motion (the 225-frame track ends where it starts).
avoidFor: You need an entrance or a reveal — this is a sustained loop, the type is fully visible from frame 0; use `kinetic-warp` for a punchy display moment.

name: rgb-glitch-text
title: RGB Glitch Text
description: Three RGB-offset text copies jitter for a few frames to create a chromatic aberration glitch
useFor: A tech, hacker, or cyberpunk scene needs a moment of digital corruption on a title.
avoidFor: You need a full text entrance animation — the glitch is a momentary effect, not a reveal; use `tracking-in` or `soft-blur-in` to bring text in.

name: rolling-number
title: Rolling Number
description: Odometer where every place rolls at its own speed, new places rising into view, settling exactly on the target value
useFor: Animating a large integer metric on a stats or milestone slide (revenue, signups, impressions).
avoidFor: The value includes a prefix or suffix like `$99` or `1.2M` — use `slot-machine-roll` which accepts arbitrary strings instead.

name: rolodex-flip
title: Rolodex Flip
description: Cycle a word through a list of values with a 3D rolodex card flip
useFor: Cycling package, feature, or value names inside a held line — install commands, "works with X" beats, plan-name cycling.
avoidFor: The values are numbers with a counting narrative — use `number-wheel` or `rolling-number`.

name: rush-type
title: Rush Type
description: White words blast into vertical RGB shutter trails generated entirely by motion
useFor: A short phrase should cycle one forceful word at a time.
avoidFor: The text must remain readable throughout the motion — use `word-push` or `zoom-words`.

name: scale-down-fade
title: Scale Down Fade
description: Subtle premium settle-in with a restrained scale-down fade on exit
useFor: A headline needs a confident, minimal entrance without any kinetic exaggeration.
avoidFor: You want energy or playfulness — the scale-down reads as composed, not exciting; use `spring-scale-in` for an overshoot bounce instead.

name: shader-text-reveal
title: Shader Text Reveal
description: Reveal words through the original OpenShaders hero material, then settle into white type
useFor: A short headline needs the hero shader reveal, one word at a time.
avoidFor: A quiet text entrance is enough — use `soft-blur-in`.

name: shadow-sweep-text
title: Shadow Sweep Text
description: A rising line is uncovered and removed by two dense dark shadow sweeps
useFor: A short statement should emerge through a dense shadow instead of fading or clipping into view.
avoidFor: The text should stay visible after entering — use `mask-reveal-up` for a one-way reveal.

name: shared-axis-y
title: Shared Axis Y
description: Per-word hard-cut staircase transition for sharp editorial phrase swaps
useFor: Swapping two text values in a slide-deck style transition (A → B → C chained in `<Sequence>`).
avoidFor: You only need to bring text in for the first time with no outgoing content — use `short-slide-down` or `staggered-fade-up` for a clean entrance instead.

name: shared-axis-z
title: Shared Axis Z
description: Scale-based shared-axis transition for focus shifts and context depth
useFor: Conveying a zoom-in narrative: moving from a broad context to a focused point.
avoidFor: The swap is a lateral topic change with no depth relationship — use `shared-axis-y` for a horizontal-edit-style cut instead.

name: sheen-slide-in
title: Sheen Slide In
description: A title glides in from the right with a long settle while a gradient sheen sweeps through the glyphs
useFor: An intro title should arrive with momentum — a fast entrance, a long exponential settle and a barely visible final creep into center.
avoidFor: You want a repeating metallic shimmer loop rather than a single arrival — use `shimmer-sweep`.

name: shimmer-sweep
title: Shimmer Sweep
description: A bright shine travels across muted text to draw attention
useFor: Highlighting a product name or pricing tier with a refined, metallic gleam — luxury SaaS, pricing slides.
avoidFor: You need the text to enter the scene — shimmer-sweep does not animate the text in; use `tracking-in` or `soft-blur-in` for the entrance, then layer a shimmer if needed.

name: short-slide-down
title: Short Slide Down
description: Words drop in from above and stack into a centered multi-line composition
useFor: A multi-word headline should build its layout visibly — each word stacking to create a composed block.
avoidFor: You are swapping between two text values — use `shared-axis-y` which handles the outgoing text exit properly.

name: short-slide-right
title: Short Slide Right
description: The whole phrase glides in from the left while words reveal in sequence through opacity
useFor: A short headline should enter with horizontal momentum — reads as forward motion or progress.
avoidFor: You are transitioning between two texts — use `shared-axis-z` (depth) or `shared-axis-y` (vertical swap) which handle the outgoing content.

name: slot-machine-roll
title: Slot Machine Roll
description: Vertical reel scrolls each character from an old value to a new value
useFor: Revealing a price change, plan upgrade, or before/after value where the string includes symbols (`$`, `%`, `×`).
avoidFor: The value is a large pure integer like `1,240,000` — use `rolling-number` which animates each decimal place independently and reads as a serious data metric.

name: soft-blur-in
title: Soft Blur In
description: Per-character fade-in with a gentle blur and upward motion
useFor: A hero headline needs the Apple-style per-character soft reveal — premium, airy, cinematic.
avoidFor: You want a hard exit animation — `soft-blur-in` is an entrance only; pair with `blur-out-up` in a `<Sequence>` for a matching exit.

name: spring-scale-in
title: Spring Scale In
description: Words pop in with a soft overshoot scale, like a spring settling into place
useFor: The scene calls for energy and bounce — product launches, celebration moments, fun CTAs.
avoidFor: The brand is serious, corporate, or premium — spring bounce reads as casual; use `scale-down-fade` or `soft-blur-in` for a composed entrance instead.

name: squeeze-in
title: Squeeze In
description: Characters appear one by one, then the whole word squeezes as the last one lands
useFor: A wordmark or short title should be uncovered by a clean wipe, as if a background-colored cover slides off it.
avoidFor: You want the whole word to collapse from a wide tracked-out state with blur — use `tracking-in`.

name: staggered-fade-up
title: Staggered Fade Up
description: Words slide up and fade in sequentially with a wave-like cascade
useFor: A headline or body sentence is long and a simpler single-unit entrance would feel flat.
avoidFor: The text is very short (1–2 words) and the stagger has nothing to reveal gradually — use `scale-down-fade` or `spring-scale-in` for a single-unit entrance with more impact.

name: stretch-in
title: Stretch In
description: Letters fly in from off-canvas and smear horizontally on the way — a vertex-lag deformation, not a scale
useFor: A heavy display word needs a fast, physical entrance where the letterforms visibly deform — bars stretch long while stems keep their exact width.
avoidFor: The type is small or body-size — the smear reads at display sizes; use `per-character-rise` for smaller text.

name: strikethrough-replace
title: Strikethrough Replace
description: Draws a strike line through the old text, then fades the new text in beneath it for an editorial correction
useFor: Showing a problem being replaced by a solution — the strike says you are crossing this out on purpose
avoidFor: There is no old text to cross out and you just need an entrance — use `staggered-fade-up` or `soft-blur-in`

name: top-down-letters
title: Top-Down Letters
description: Letters descend from above in a pronounced staircase, one symbol at a time
useFor: A single uppercase word or short acronym should enter with structural weight — each letter landing like a stamp.
avoidFor: The text is more than ~8 characters — many letters dropping sequentially stretches the animation and the last letters feel delayed; use `staggered-fade-up` for longer phrases.

name: tracking-in
title: Tracking In
description: Letter-spacing collapses and blur clears with a springy entrance
useFor: A title word or brand name should feel like it is focusing into place — tracking collapse is the right metaphor for clarity, precision, or sharpness.
avoidFor: You want per-character stagger — `tracking-in` moves all letters as one unit; use `soft-blur-in` for a per-character blur-and-rise stagger instead.

name: type-fossil
title: Type Fossil
description: A readable word carries layers of fine contours, revises itself, then compresses into a clean typographic imprint
useFor: A creative process should move from earlier wording to a finished idea.
avoidFor: Letters must morph individually between phrases — use kinetic-morph-text.

name: typed-split-wipe
title: Typed Split Wipe
description: A centered cursorless type build exits through opposing fixed-layout glyph wipes
useFor: A product or feature introduction should type itself cleanly before breaking into controlled directional fragments.
avoidFor: You need a conventional typewriter with a blinking caret and no exit — use `typewriter`.

name: typewriter
title: Typewriter
description: Character-by-character text reveal with a deterministic blinking cursor
useFor: Simulating a command being typed into a terminal or input — pairs with `terminal-simulator`.
avoidFor: The text is long — typing a paragraph at a readable speed eats far more frames than a viewer will wait; use `staggered-fade-up` or `blur-out-up` instead.

name: value-swap
title: Value Swap
description: Swap a value in place with a vertical slide so the layout never shifts
useFor: A value changes at a specific story beat — before/after price, status promotion, a hex/token flip.
avoidFor: Values should cycle continuously as a montage — use `rolodex-flip` with its own rhythm instead.

name: word-push
title: Word Push
description: Words drive in from the right and push the line left into its new center
useFor: A single tagline or closing phrase should build word by word with physical, push-driven motion instead of plain fades.
avoidFor: Several phrases must play in sequence with cuts between them — use `word-stream` for the multi-phrase flow.

name: word-stream
title: Word Stream
description: Voiceover-paced phrases building word by word while the line drifts left
useFor: An intro or narration follows a voiceover and each phrase should build word by word at speaking pace.
avoidFor: There is only one static phrase to reveal — use `per-word-crossfade` for a single calm word-by-word entrance.

name: zoom-words
title: Zoom Words
description: Huge words fade into a long line while the camera rides the write head
useFor: An intro should open uncomfortably close: huge words appearing one by one while the camera tracks the growing line off-frame.
avoidFor: The whole phrase must fit the frame at rest — use `per-word-crossfade` or `word-stream`.

name: accordion
title: Accordion
description: An accordion panel whose open/closed state is a pure function of the timeline
useFor: Showing a collapsible FAQ or settings section expanding on a timeline cue.
avoidFor: The content is always visible — there is no collapse state; lay it out statically instead.

name: ai-prompt-flow
title: AI Prompt Flow
description: A full prompt-to-answer scene — the prompt types itself, the button runs to loading, a skeleton reveals, and the answer crossfades in
useFor: Demoing an AI product's whole prompt-to-answer experience in one self-contained scene
avoidFor: You only need a button press with a loading state — use `button` with `state="loading"`

name: alert-dialog
title: AlertDialog
description: A modal alert dialog whose opened/closed state is a pure function of the timeline
useFor: Showing a destructive confirmation dialog (delete, reset, revoke) in a product demo.
avoidFor: The action is non-destructive or form-based — use `dialog` instead.

name: blur-in
title: Blur In
description: A wrapper that reveals a single child with blur, opacity, and a directional offset
useFor: Revealing an arbitrary JSX subtree (card, image, composed scene) with a premium blur entrance.
avoidFor: You're animating a text-only line — use a purpose-built text reveal (`soft-blur-in`, `staggered-fade-up`) instead of wrapping raw text.

name: button
title: Button
description: A button whose visual state is a pure function of the timeline
useFor: Showing the full interactive lifecycle of a CTA — hover → press → loading → success — on the timeline.
avoidFor: You need a selectable row inside a menu — use `dropdown-menu-item` or `command-menu-item` instead.

name: caret
title: Caret
description: A blinking text caret — a pure motion atom or a fully controlled bar
useFor: Placing a blinking insertion cursor beside a text node or at the end of a typed string.
avoidFor: You need the full input UX (focus ring, border, value reveal) — use `input` instead, which owns its own caret.

name: chat-flow
title: Chat Flow
description: A messaging conversation that types outgoing messages, shows typing indicators, and pops in incoming replies with reactions
useFor: A scene needs a messaging conversation that carries your own brand tokens instead of a real platform's chrome.
avoidFor: The video must read as Telegram — use `telegram-chat-flow`, which owns the tailed bubbles, in-bubble timestamps, and double-check marks.

name: checkbox
title: Checkbox
description: A checkbox whose checked/unchecked state is a pure function of the timeline
useFor: Showing a task being checked off in a to-do or onboarding list.
avoidFor: The choice is mutually exclusive within a group — use `radio` instead.

name: checkout-flow
title: CheckoutFlow
description: A cursor-driven checkout card with a pricing toggle, card input, terms checkbox, and payment confirmation
useFor: Demoing a SaaS payment or upgrade UX end-to-end with cursor navigation and toast confirmation.
avoidFor: You only need a payment form without cursor animation — compose `field`, `input`, `button` manually.

name: combobox
title: Combobox
description: A searchable select with a typed-query input, filtered panel, and row selection
useFor: Showing a searchable/filterable dropdown with a typed query narrowing the list on the timeline.
avoidFor: The list is not filterable and selection is direct — use `select` (non-filterable dropdown) instead.

name: command-menu
title: Command Menu
description: A keyboard-driven command palette with backdrop, typing animation, and row selection
useFor: Demoing a ⌘K palette opening with a typed query filtering icon-labeled commands.
avoidFor: The list has no icons or keyboard shortcuts and is triggered from a button — use `dropdown-menu` instead.

name: context-menu
title: Context Menu
description: A right-click menu panel that opens at the cursor point with no built-in trigger
useFor: Showing a right-click menu appearing at a cursor position over content in a product demo.
avoidFor: The menu is triggered from a button in the UI — use `dropdown-menu` instead.

name: cursor
title: Cursor
description: An animated cursor that follows a scripted path with click ripple and press effects
useFor: Guiding the viewer's attention through a UI by animating a pointer between elements.
avoidFor: You need a blinking text insertion cursor — use `caret` instead.

name: dialog
title: Dialog
description: A modal dialog whose opened/closed state is a pure function of the timeline
useFor: Showing a non-destructive modal (edit form, settings, profile update) opening and closing on the timeline.
avoidFor: The action is irreversible or destructive — use `alert-dialog` instead.

name: drawer
title: Drawer
description: A bottom panel whose opened/closed state is a pure function of the timeline
useFor: Showing a mobile-style bottom sheet sliding up from the edge of the frame.
avoidFor: The overlay should be a centered modal — use `dialog` instead.

name: dropdown-menu
title: DropdownMenu
description: A dropdown menu container with opened/closed states and action rows
useFor: Showing a button that opens an action list — the classic "Options" or account menu pattern.
avoidFor: The menu is invoked by right-click at a cursor position — use `context-menu` instead.

name: field
title: Field
description: A static layout family for composing labeled form controls with consistent vertical spacing
useFor: Laying out labeled form controls — label, animated control, description hint — with consistent spacing
avoidFor: You need the control itself to animate — `field` is layout only; put `input` or `button` inside it

name: imessage-chat-flow
title: iMessage Chat Flow
description: iMessage-styled conversation with gray incoming and blue outgoing bubbles, typing indicator, Delivered label, and tapback reactions
useFor: The scene must read as iMessage — gray incoming and blue outgoing tailed bubbles with tapback badges at the outer top corner.
avoidFor: The scene must read as Telegram — use `telegram-chat-flow` for in-bubble timestamps, double-check marks, and reaction chips.

name: input
title: Input
description: An input field whose visual state is a pure function of the timeline
useFor: Showing a text field being focused, typed into, or validated at a specific frame.
avoidFor: The trigger needs to open a searchable list — use `combobox` instead (which wraps input internally).

name: message-bubble
title: Message Bubble
description: A state-driven speech bubble with incoming and outgoing variants and an optional reaction badge
useFor: You are hand-timing a single message landing on a beat you control, driving `style` from `useMessageBubbleTransition`.
avoidFor: You want a whole scripted conversation with a composer, typing beats, and reactions — use `chat-flow`, which schedules bubbles for you.

name: onboarding-stepper-flow
title: Onboarding Stepper Flow
description: A multi-step onboarding scene where a stepper advances through form panels and finishes on a success state
useFor: Demoing a multi-step onboarding experience — account setup, plan choice, preferences — in one scene
avoidFor: The flow is a payment checkout — use `checkout-flow`, which is cursor-driven with card entry and a toast

name: popover
title: Popover
description: A floating card that appears beside an anchor with arbitrary content
useFor: Showing a hover-card with richer content (title + description) than a single-line tooltip label allows.
avoidFor: You only need a single-line label — use `tooltip` instead (lighter, no title/description structure).

name: progress
title: Progress
description: A progress bar that fills along a scripted numeric value timeline
useFor: Showing a loading, upload, or completion bar animating to a target value.
avoidFor: The state is binary (done/not done) — use `switch` instead.

name: radio
title: Radio
description: A radio whose checked/unchecked state is a pure function of the timeline
useFor: Demonstrating a single-choice selection moment in a form walkthrough.
avoidFor: The control is binary on/off — use `switch` instead (sliding thumb reads more naturally for toggles).

name: resizable
title: Resizable
description: A two-panel split container whose divider ratio and handle state are driven by a scripted dual-channel timeline
useFor: Demonstrating a code/preview split pane layout with its ratio animating across frames.
avoidFor: You need fixed-width layout panels — plain CSS grid or flex avoids the drag-state overhead entirely.

name: select
title: Select
description: A dropdown select container with opened/closed states and item panel
useFor: Demonstrating a dropdown menu opening and an option being highlighted or selected on the timeline.
avoidFor: You only need to show one item row in isolation — use `select-item` directly without the panel overhead.

name: select-menu
title: Select Menu
description: A vertical option list whose highlight slides between selections on the timeline
useFor: A vertical single-choice menu where one option is highlighted and the highlight should glide smoothly between options as the selection changes.
avoidFor: Options must open a reveal panel — use `select` instead.

name: settings-toggle-flow
title: SettingsToggleFlow
description: Two-column settings card with a blur-in entrance and a cursor-driven switch, select, slider, and save
useFor: Showing a complete settings interaction walkthrough for a product demo — zero assembly required.
avoidFor: You need only one control type — use `switch`, `select`, or `slider` individually instead.

name: sheet
title: Sheet
description: A side panel whose opened/closed state is a pure function of the timeline
useFor: Showing a slide-in edit panel or settings drawer with backdrop dim in a product demo.
avoidFor: You need a full blocking modal with centered placement — use `alert-dialog` instead.

name: signup-flow
title: SignupFlow
description: A cursor-driven signup card — labeled fields fill top-to-bottom, then submit with success feedback
useFor: Showing a full onboarding or signup flow in a product launch or demo video.
avoidFor: You need a generic form with custom fields — compose `input` + `button` + `cursor` manually instead.

name: skeleton
title: Skeleton
description: A shimmer placeholder that crossfades to real content when loaded
useFor: Showing a loading state resolving to real content — the skeleton fades out as real UI fades in.
avoidFor: You only need a single shimmer rectangle — use `skeleton-block` directly (no state API, no crossfade overhead).

name: skeleton-block
title: Skeleton Block
description: A single shimmer placeholder rectangle whose highlight sweep is a pure function of the frame
useFor: Building a custom skeleton layout by composing individual shimmer rectangles at precise dimensions
avoidFor: You want shimmer and real content to crossfade automatically — use `skeleton`, which takes a loading/loaded state and children

name: slider
title: Slider
description: A range slider with a draggable thumb driven by a scripted value and thumb-state timeline
useFor: Demonstrating a range control being dragged to a target value with hover/press thumb states.
avoidFor: You need to show completion percentage with no thumb — use `progress` instead (fill-only, no interaction states).

name: spinner
title: Spinner
description: A deterministic spinning arc — pure function of the Remotion frame
useFor: Showing a loading indicator inside a button after a click (hover → press → loading state).
avoidFor: You need a full-width loading bar with a track — use `progress` instead.

name: stepper
title: Stepper
description: A multi-step progress indicator that advances along a scripted numeric position timeline
useFor: Showing a multi-step onboarding, checkout, or wizard flow advancing through numbered steps.
avoidFor: Steps have no sequential order — use `tabs` instead (tab switching without numbered connectors).

name: switch
title: Switch
description: A switch whose checked/unchecked state is a pure function of the timeline
useFor: Showing a toggle being flipped in a settings panel walkthrough.
avoidFor: The choice is one of multiple mutually exclusive options — use `radio` or `select` instead.

name: tabs
title: Tabs
description: A tabs widget whose active-tab state is a pure function of the timeline
useFor: Showing a tabbed UI switching between content panels in a product demo.
avoidFor: Steps are sequential and ordered — use `stepper` instead (numbered connectors + check marks).

name: telegram-chat-flow
title: Telegram Chat Flow
description: Telegram-styled conversation with tailed bubbles, delivery checks, typing status, and reaction chips
useFor: The scene must read as Telegram — blue tailed bubbles, in-bubble timestamps, and double-check delivery marks.
avoidFor: The scene must read as iMessage — use `imessage-chat-flow` for gray incoming bubbles, the Delivered label, and tapback badges.

name: toast
title: Toast
description: A notification that slides in from below, holds, then auto-dismisses
useFor: Showing a success/error notification appear after an action (form submit, save, API call).
avoidFor: The feedback is persistent and must not auto-dismiss — use a banner or inline alert component instead.

name: toggle-group
title: Toggle Group
description: A segmented control whose active value slides a thumb indicator between segments
useFor: Showing a segmented control switching between view modes, time ranges, or mutually exclusive options.
avoidFor: You need content panels that crossfade below the control — use `tabs` instead (full panel area + indicator).

name: tooltip
title: Tooltip
description: A small floating label that appears above an anchor on hover
useFor: Showing a hover tooltip appearing next to a UI element in a product walkthrough.
avoidFor: You need title + description in the overlay — use `popover` instead (richer two-field content with optional children).

name: typing-indicator
title: Typing Indicator
description: A motion atom that renders N bouncing dots driven directly by useCurrentFrame
useFor: Signalling that a reply or an answer is being composed — drop it inside a `message-bubble` or any container.
avoidFor: The wait is an async operation rather than a conversation — use `spinner`, or `skeleton` when the placeholder resolves to content.

name: animated-bar-chart
title: Animated Bar Chart
description: Bars spring up from the baseline with a staggered cascade
useFor: Showing comparative categorical metrics in a product demo — feature usage, plan distribution, benchmark scores.
avoidFor: The data represents change over time — continuous trends belong in `animated-line-chart`, not bars.

name: animated-line-chart
title: Animated Line Chart
description: A line chart whose path draws on from left to right
useFor: Showing growth or trend over time — revenue curve, DAU climb, error-rate drop.
avoidFor: The data is categorical (not time-ordered) — use `animated-bar-chart` to compare discrete values side by side.

name: check-list
title: Check List
description: A handwritten checklist that writes itself out, then ticks and strikes through every done item
useFor: A list of features, steps, or done-items should be read in full and then crossed off in a hand-made scene.
avoidFor: Labels need to wrap across lines, or the list needs numbering or nesting. One label, one line.

name: glass-code-block
title: Glass Code Block
description: A premium frosted-glass code editor window with a regex tokenizer and line-by-line stagger reveal
useFor: A landing or hero scene needs an animated code backdrop that reads as "premium dev tool."
avoidFor: The scene requires the code to be visibly typed out character by character — use `terminal-simulator` or `typewriter` instead.

name: glass-code-walk
title: Glass Code Walk
description: A camera that scans a glass code block top to bottom as it types, then pulls back to a centered hold
useFor: A code reveal needs camera motion — the frame stays pinned to the line currently typing, then pulls back so the whole file lands as the payoff.
avoidFor: The code panel should sit still in frame with no camera move — use `glass-code-block`, which this component wraps and animates.

name: paper-sticker
title: Paper Sticker
description: A taped paper chip that slaps onto the scene over two stop-motion poses
useFor: Short labels, chips, or callout notes should exist as physical taped paper on a stop-motion scene.
avoidFor: The content is long text or looks like interactive UI — this is a paper prop, not a component sim.

name: polaroid
title: Polaroid
description: An instant-photo frame with a handwritten caption for video, images, or live compositions
useFor: Media belongs in a hand-placed instant-photo frame with a handwritten caption.
avoidFor: You just need a plain rounded video frame with no paper story — use `backdrop` with padding.

name: reel
title: Reel
description: A fixed centered card where images stack on the z-axis and each blooms open over the last
useFor: Showing a sequence of screenshots or product shots that should bloom open one over the last in a fixed frame.
avoidFor: You need a single framed photo rather than a sequence — use `polaroid` instead.

name: search-reveal
title: Search Reveal
description: Construction circles expand into a search field, type your product name, and reveal an abstract graphic panel
useFor: A product introduction should begin with a search for its name.
avoidFor: Words should fly and morph between phrases — use `kinetic-morph-text`.

name: terminal-cursor-zoom
title: Terminal Cursor Zoom
description: Camera locked to the typing cursor, dollying across a terminal as a command types at high zoom
useFor: One install command is the whole beat and it must stay legible in a vertical or small-screen crop — the camera holds the cursor at frame center at 2.8× zoom.
avoidFor: The session has multiple lines, logs, or success output — use `terminal-simulator`; this component types exactly one command line and the camera never leaves it.

name: terminal-simulator
title: Terminal Simulator
description: A console window that types out commands and rolls older lines off the top
useFor: Demoing a CLI tool install sequence (`npm install`, `npx shadcn add`, build output).
avoidFor: You only need to type a single short string — use `typewriter` instead, which is lighter and pairs with any layout.
